note: Dated regulatory reference data (drone/operations-reference spec). Every value carries its citation, effective date, the date it was last checked against the authority (reviewed), and a status. Proposed rules are never treated as in force. Re-verify any entry whose review date is more than 12 months old; the build warns.

entries.meaning: Maximum altitude above ground level, unless within a 400 ft radius of a structure and no higher than 400 ft above its immediate uppermost limit
Maximum groundspeed (100 mph)
Minimum flight visibility from the control station, statute miles
Minimum distance below clouds
Minimum horizontal distance from clouds
A small unmanned aircraft weighs less than 55 lb at takeoff, including everything on board
Category 2 operations over people: no injury more severe than that from 11 ft-lb of kinetic energy transferred from a rigid object
Operators must comply with Remote ID; FAA enforcement discretion ended March 16, 2024

entries.citation: Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems Beyond Visual Line of Sight Operations, 90 FR 38212 (August 7, 2025), docket FAA-2025-1908
entries.meaning: Proposed Part 108 for BVLOS operations. Comment period reopened January 28, 2026; no final rule published as of the review date
Maximum height from the closest point of the surface of the earth in the open category
Maximum take-off mass in the open category, less than 25 kg
Class C1: MTOM less than 900 g, or transferred energy under 80 J in a head-on impact at terminal velocity
National standard scenarios expired on December 31, 2025; standard scenarios (STS) require class C5 or C6

entries.citation: EASA, Guidelines for UAS operations in the open and specific category, Issue 03 (17 July 2025) (VLOS distance: ALOS and DLOS)
entries.meaning: ALOS = 327 × CD + 20 m (multirotor), 490 × CD + 30 m (fixed wing); DLOS = 0.3 × ground visibility; VLOS = the smaller. US Part 107 sets no numeric VLOS distance
Airplane VFR by day: fuel to the first point of intended landing, then at least 30 minutes at normal cruising speed
Airplane VFR at night: fuel to the first point of intended landing, then at least 45 minutes at normal cruising speed
Rotorcraft VFR: fuel to the first point of intended landing, then at least 20 minutes at normal cruising speed
IFR: fuel to the first airport of intended landing, then to the alternate when one is required, then 45 minutes at normal cruising speed
Helicopter IFR: fuel to the first airport of intended landing, then to the alternate when one is required, then 30 minutes at normal cruising speed

Below 18,000 ft MSL, set the current reported altimeter setting; at and above it, 29.92 inHg. Paragraph (b) gives the lowest usable flight level by altimeter setting, from FL180 at 29.92 inHg or higher to FL210 at 27.41 through 26.92

To carry passengers from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise, the pilot in command needs, within the preceding 90 days, at least three takeoffs and three landings to a full stop in that period, as sole manipulator of the controls, in the same category, class, and type (if a type rating is required). Counted here as current through the 90th day after the oldest of the three most recent qualifying takeoffs and of the three most recent qualifying landings

Digital modulation in 2400-2483.5 MHz: at most 1 W (30 dBm) conducted into an antenna of up to 6 dBi, the conducted power reduced dB for dB above 6 dBi, so at most 36 dBm EIRP (fixed point-to-point links may use more gain under (c)(1)(i))
Wideband data transmission in the 2.4 GHz band: RF output power, defined as mean e.i.r.p., at most 20 dBm

entries.citation: ALTA/NSPS Minimum Standard Detail Requirements (2026), Section 3.E.v
entries.meaning: Maximum allowable Relative Positional Precision between adjacent boundary corners: 2 cm (0.07 feet) plus 50 parts per million of the direct distance, as the semi-major axis of the 95% error ellipse (Section 3.E.i)
